acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE DESIGN QUESTION IS ANSWERED IN WRITING BEFORE ANY EDIT: are `@emitted_floor`, `@go_tag_floor` and the `@barkpark_family_keys` pair meant to be ratchets (`>=`, tolerate growth) or acknowledgement gates (`==`, force a human to notice growth)? Both are defensible and they produce different work. Record the answer and its owner. A repair that silently converts `==` to `>=` without that ruling is REFUSED -- it would delete a gate someone built on purpose.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET. RULING B, from the lead, recorded in writing and its owner named: KEEP `==`, kill the ambush, rename the attributes. The decisive evidence is in the census's OWN refusal text at the go-tag arm -- `>=` was already tried and already let a defect through: '#10474 shipped one tag of slack under the old `>=`'. So `==` is bidirectional ON PURPOSE (FEWER = the scanner broke; MORE = a key landed unannounced) and converting it would look like a cleanup while silently deleting half the coverage. I did NOT convert it. I proposed B and the lead ruled B; the reasoning is in PR #12972's first section.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: NO PIN IS DERIVED FROM THE CORPUS IT MEASURES. Whatever ships, a reviewer can point at each remaining number and say what would make it red. A floor computed from the tree it bounds is vacuous by construction; state explicitly for each of the seven pins whether it stayed pinned and why.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET, and stated per pin. NOTHING IS DERIVED FROM THE CORPUS IT MEASURES. @go_tag_pinned, @emitted_pinned, @barkpark_family_keys and @barkpark_family_keys_blind all remain COMMITTED LITERALS asserted with `==`; @go_tag_sites remains a committed map; @corpus_floor (both files) and @register_floor remain `>=` ratchets, untouched and correctly named. What each would red on: a scalar pin reds when its measured expression moves in EITHER direction; the register reds on any multiplicity change; the ratchets red on a shrink. THE ONE THING THAT IS RESOLVED FROM SOURCE IS AN ANCHOR, NOT A BOUND: the reader census's control line, which is the const's own text -- and the distinction is load-bearing, since a bound computed from what it bounds can never red. That distinction is written into the new arm's comment so the next reader cannot repeat the mistake I was nearly instructed to make.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE LINE PIN STOPS BEING A LINE NUMBER. reader_less_instrument_census_test.exs:803 anchors on the control's TEXT (`const requestStatsPath`) rather than `&1.line == 659`, and its refusal distinguishes 'the anchor moved' from 'the control is gone' by name -- `expected <text> at :N, found <other>`. Any edit above that const in internal/agent/report.go must leave the arm green; prove it by INSERTING lines above it and re-running.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET, MUTATION-PROVED IN THREE DIRECTIONS. reader_less_instrument_census_test.exs now carries @control_file + @control_text (~S(const requestStatsPath = "/v1/instance/request-stats")) and control_line/0, which returns {:ok, line} | {:error, why} and never raises, so the arm names WHICH half broke. THE INSERTION PROOF THIS CRITERION DEMANDS: 20 lines inserted above the const in internal/agent/report.go moved it 659 -> 679 and the arm stayed GREEN at 17 tests / 0 failures. THE COUNTERFACTUAL, on that same padded tree: reverting the assertion to the old `&1.line == 659` gives 17 tests, 1 FAILURE -- so the green descends from the anchor change and not from the tree. BOTH HALVES STILL RED BY NAME: renaming the const away yields 'THE CONTROL TEXT IS GONE ... the control text does not occur in internal/agent/report.go at all'; blinding the scanner to that one file yields 'THE SCANNER MISSED A LINE THAT IS THERE ... The line was RESOLVED by reading internal/agent/report.go, never transcribed'. The two failures the single number used to conflate now print different sentences.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: EVERY PROSE SITE STATING A PINNED FACT IS CORRECTED, AND THE COUNT OF THEM IS REPORTED. At minimum the four found here: reader census :25, :63 and :659 (all say report.go:639; the const is at :659) and payload census :1200-1203 ('59 keys ... 45 without' above attributes reading 62 and 46). Re-derive the list rather than trusting this one -- it was assembled by grep and a grep can miss a spelling.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET, ALL FOUR NAMED SITES, AND THE WIDER SWEEP REPORTED RATHER THAN SILENTLY DROPPED. FIXED (4/4 of this criterion's stated minimum): reader census moduledoc :25 and :63 and register rationale :659 all restated `report.go:639` and now name `const requestStatsPath` with no line at all; payload census :1208 read '59 keys with the :when unwrap, 45 without' while the two attributes four lines below it read 62 and 46 -- it now states the INVARIANT (the :when unwrap is worth exactly the 14 vitals, and the two counts must move INDEPENDENTLY) instead of restating numbers that live once each below it. A CORRECTION AGAINST MYSELF: I first stamped this criterion with only 3 of the 4 fixed, having overlooked the payload site while chasing the wider sweep. Caught on re-reading my own evidence before reporting; the fourth landed as e8b59975ba. || THE COUNT, RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN TRUSTED, as this criterion demands: I swept every file:line claim in BOTH files -- 46 claims, 39 resolving to a unique file, 7 ambiguous basenames -- and printed the line each actually points at. BEYOND the four pinned-fact sites, roughly ten CITATIONS are wrong on main today: api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex:1633 and internal/cli/cloud_support_cmd.go:1460 are BLANK LINES; cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/platform_delivery.ex:356 is a bare `end`. I did NOT correct those, and the reason is a finding against my own instrument: I SELF-TESTED THE SWEEP ON THE KNOWN POSITIVE AND IT FAILED -- run against the pre-fix tree it reports report.go:639 as in-range and non-blank, because on that tree line 639 held ordinary code. 'In range and non-blank' is not 'correct'. So the sweep is a review aid that surfaces candidates, never a staleness detector, and correcting ten citations by hand with an instrument that cannot verify its own work would manufacture a green I could not stand behind. Reported in PR #12972 and left for a follow-up that builds a real arm.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: SECOND-ROUND PINS CANNOT AMBUSH THE NEXT BUILDER. One run reports EVERY pin that has moved, with its measured value, instead of surfacing `@emitted_floor` and `@barkpark_family_keys` only after the emit side is fixed. Demonstrate on a real two-field change: apply it, run once, and show the single output naming all moved pins.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET, AND DEMONSTRATED ON A REAL TWO-FIELD CHANGE AS WRITTEN. New arm 'PIN CO-EDIT: every moved pin is named in ONE run, with the value to write' measures all four scalar pins by the SAME expressions their per-pin arms use, plus the @go_tag_sites register as MOVED-or-not. M5 (two pins perturbed to their pre-#12967 values) produces THREE failures: the two per-pin arms red separately and tell you nothing about each other -- that IS the ambush -- while the co-edit arm names BOTH in one place: '@emitted_pinned 149 -> 151' and '@barkpark_family_keys 60 -> 62'. M4 (two NEW Go json tags added to SiteDeleteResult in internal/cloudclient/client.go): '@go_tag_pinned 275 -> 277'. M6 (one new tag name + one duplicate of an existing name): '1 of 4 scalar pin(s) no longer match this tree, and the SITE register moved too', naming '@go_tag_pinned 275 -> 276' and '@go_tag_sites MOVED'. I added the register line specifically because without it the arm would promise 'every moved pin' and mean 'every moved SCALAR pin' -- the same over-promise it exists to stop.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: MUTATION-PROVED, EACH ARM SEPARATELY, WITH RUN OUTPUT. For every arm touched: break the property it guards and watch THAT arm red by name, then restore and watch it green. Specifically `@barkpark_family_keys_blind` must be shown to still measure the blind walker INDEPENDENTLY -- move the seeing count and prove blind does not follow. An arm that cannot be made to fail is decoration.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: MET. Every arm touched was made to fail and then restored, with run output, listed in PR #12972's mutation table: M1 (insert above the const -> green, 17/0), M1' (old line pin on the padded tree -> 17 tests 1 failure), M2 (control text gone -> half one reds by name), M3 (scanner blinded -> half two reds by name), M4/M5/M6 (the co-edit arm reds naming exactly the moved pins). THE TWIN'S INDEPENDENCE, WHICH THIS CRITERION SINGLES OUT: under M5 I moved @barkpark_family_keys (the SEEING count) and @barkpark_family_keys_blind did NOT follow -- it is computed by its own expression (`unwrap_when: false`) and appeared as unmoved in the same report. The pre-existing arm that pins the loss to EXACTLY the pressure block (`assert "cpu_percent" in emitted(pressure()).keys` / `refute ... unwrap_when: false`) is untouched, so the blind-spot measurement is intact in both directions. FULL SUITE: cloud 3733 tests / 0 failures; mix format --check-formatted clean.

THE CLUSTER, RE-DERIVED FROM origin/main 39bc687d19 BY READING THE FILES, not transcribed from the report that prompted it. Adding TWO Go struct fields on #12967 moved FIVE pinned numbers across two files. The pins are the defect; the numbers were all correct when written.

THE SHARPEST FACT, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THAT WAS REPORTED. Three attributes NAMED _floor are asserted with ==, not >=:

  payload_key_set_census_test.exs:1274   assert total_emitted([]) == @emitted_floor
  payload_key_set_census_test.exs:1341   assert MapSet.size(Go.all_tags(src)) == @go_tag_floor
  payload_key_set_census_test.exs:1264-5 assert seeing == @barkpark_family_keys
                                         assert blind  == @barkpark_family_keys_blind

A FLOOR THAT IS AN EQUALITY IS NOT A FLOOR. It reds on honest GROWTH as loudly as on the scanner breaking, and the refusal text says so out loud -- "floor is EXACTLY 275" -- while the attribute keeps a name that promises a lower bound. Two files in the same tree DO use real ratchets and prove the distinction is available and understood: @corpus_floor (:2149, >=) and reader_less_instrument_census_test.exs @register_floor (:752, >=), @corpus_floor (:789, >=).

Whether the == is a DEFECT or a DELIBERATE two-directional gate is an open design question and this row does not presume it. The refusal at :1343 argues for deliberate -- "either the TAG SCANNER is broken (fewer) or [you added keys]" -- i.e. the equality exists to force a human to acknowledge growth. If that is the intent, THE NAME IS THE DEFECT and the co-edit cost is the thing to fix, not the operator. Decide before building.

TODAY'S VALUES ON MAIN, read from the files:

  @emitted_floor              151     ==   payload census
  @go_tag_floor               275     ==   payload census
  @barkpark_family_keys        62     ==   payload census
  @barkpark_family_keys_blind  46     ==   payload census
  @corpus_floor               550     >=   payload census      (a real ratchet)
  @register_floor               9     >=   reader census       (a real ratchet)
  @corpus_floor               400     >=   reader census       (a real ratchet)
  @go_tag_sites               map     --   payload census      (SITE multiplicity register, partitioned against @go_tag_floor at :1565)

SECOND-ROUND PINS ARE THE EXPENSIVE PART. @emitted_floor and @barkpark_family_keys only move once the EMIT side is corrected, so they arrive after the builder believes they are done. The file's own rule -- "Re-measure BOTH by the 999-technique on this tree; never by arithmetic" -- is correct and is also the whole problem: the technique is set both floors to 999, run, read the two refusal lines, edit, repeat. FOUR ROUNDS OF THAT is the real cost, and nothing forces them to arrive together.

THE LINE PIN, AND IT IS WORSE THAN REPORTED. The reader census's control is internal/agent/report.go. The line is stated in FIVE places and #12967 corrected only the TWO the test executes:

  :803   assert ... &1.line == 659      <- CORRECTED by #12967
  :805   failure message ...:659        <- CORRECTED by #12967
  :25    moduledoc  report.go:639     <- STALE
  :63    moduledoc  report.go:639     <- STALE
  :659   register row rationale :639    <- STALE

const requestStatsPath is at report.go:659 on main today, verified by git show origin/main:internal/agent/report.go | grep -n. So the executable half is right and the three halves a HUMAN reads are wrong. Anyone reading the moduledoc to understand the control is sent to the wrong line -- and nothing can ever tell them, because prose has no assertion behind it. This is the same shape as pds-w37 and as the D448 selftest arm: THE PART A CHECK REACHES GETS FIXED, THE PART A READER REACHES ROTS.

A FOURTH STALE PROSE SITE, in the payload census at :1200-1203: "59 keys with the :when unwrap, 45 without", sitting directly above @barkpark_family_keys 62 and @barkpark_family_keys_blind 46. Both moved; the sentence describing them did not.

THE TWIN THAT MUST NOT MOVE. @barkpark_family_keys_blind counts the walker that puts the ATTRIBUTE rather than the literal keys. Any repair must leave its independence intact -- a fix that makes it track the seeing count destroys the blind-spot measurement the pair exists to take, silently and in the green direction. Its independence is the acceptance test for the repair, not a footnote.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, and it is the obvious move: DO NOT DERIVE THESE FLOORS FROM THE CORPUS THEY MEASURE. A ratchet whose bound is computed from the thing it bounds can never red. That is the opposite of the D448 selftest repair (#12966), where the derived number was a value the test INJECTED, not one it measured -- and the distinction is the whole reason that repair was sound and this one cannot copy it verbatim.
